title: Air-Fryer Salmon Fillet
subtitle: Glazed salmon fillets cooked in the air fryer in 10 minutes
excerpt: Salmon fillets brushed with a honey and soy glaze, cooked in the air fryer until the glaze is caramelised and the fish is just set through. On the table in 15 minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Salmon is one of the best fish for the air fryer because its high fat content keeps the flesh moist during the blast of dry heat. The air fryer produces a result closer to grilling than baking: the top of the fillet colours quickly and the glaze caramelises without burning if the temperature is right. Skin-on fillets hold together better and the skin goes slightly crisp.

recipeTools.notes: Any air fryer large enough to hold 2 fillets side by side.

content.text: The glaze goes on after the first 5 minutes of cooking, not at the start. Adding it too early causes it to burn before the fish is cooked through. Press the thickest part of the fillet: it should give slightly but not feel raw. Salmon is best served just set at the centre rather than cooked through completely.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, lemon juice, and garlic together to make the glaze. Preheat the air fryer to 200 C for 2 minutes.
Place the salmon fillets skin-side down in the air fryer basket. Season with black pepper. Cook for 5 minutes.
Brush the glaze over the top of the fillets generously. Cook for a further 4 to 5 minutes until the glaze is caramelised and the fish is just set through.
Serve immediately with rice or a green salad.
